chosen.premise: Nidorina’s head horn has atrophied, apparently so her children won’t be poked while she feeds them.
chosen.hook: Nidorina may have lost her horn to protect her babies.
chosen.visualIdea: Show a horned Nidoran♀ fading into horn-atrophied Nidorina beside a mother feeding her young.
chosen.note: Highly distinctive and surprising, with a strong evolution visual. The evidence says the horn has atrophied and that this is thought to protect offspring, so 'lost her horn' slightly overstates the claim.

candidates.premise: To feed her young, Nidorina chews food into a tender paste before spitting it out for them.
candidates.hook: Nidorina prepares baby food in the strangest way possible.
candidates.visualIdea: Show food entering Nidorina’s mouth, becoming paste, then being delivered to waiting offspring.
candidates.note: Extremely concrete, directly supported, and visually clear. It is memorable, though the gross-out angle may narrow its emotional appeal.

candidates.premise: Nidorina’s body barbs reveal her mood: tucked away with family, raised when threatened, and retracted while resting.
candidates.hook: Nidorina’s spikes are basically a mood ring.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate Nidorina’s barbs retracting around family, then snapping upright as a danger warning.
candidates.note: A well-supported, easily animated behavior system, though 'mood ring' is a familiar framing and the premise combines several related entries.

candidates.premise: When Nidorina’s group is threatened, they band together and attack with a chorus of ultrasonic waves.
candidates.hook: Threaten one Nidorina, and the whole group starts singing.
candidates.visualIdea: A danger signal spreads through a Nidorina group as concentric ultrasonic wave rings combine.
candidates.note: Group defense by ultrasonic waves is distinctive and cinematic. 'Starts singing' is catchy but softens the more precise idea of a coordinated ultrasonic attack.

candidates.premise: Nidorina keeps her barbs tucked around family but becomes nervous when separated from them.
candidates.hook: Nidorina’s safest defense turns off around the people she loves.
candidates.visualIdea: Split-screen: tucked barbs in a family group, then raised-alert posture as Nidorina stands alone.
candidates.note: The family-versus-separation contrast is compelling and supported, but 'people she loves' anthropomorphizes the entries and overlaps with the broader barb mechanic.

candidates.premise: Nidorina is gentle and reluctant to fight, yet prefers clawing and biting over relying on her slowly growing horn.
candidates.hook: Nidorina avoids fighting—but if forced, she bites first.
candidates.visualIdea: Contrast a slowly growing horn with quick claw-and-bite attack silhouettes.
candidates.note: The gentle-but-physical contradiction is supported, but the horn comparison is more about slow development than a direct combat choice, making the premise slightly compressed.

rounds.request: N/A—horn-sacrifice is strong enough for the episode. Sharpen the wording to 'Nidorina’s horn atrophied—possibly to keep her babies safe while feeding them,' avoiding the stronger but unsupported claim that she simply lost it.
